hunks.sol: Mujin hoisted the unconscious Jin Taekyung onto his back.

hunks.baseline: It had only been a few days since Jopil’s brutal palm strike had left him with internal injuries. He had loudly told Jin Taekyung he was almost fully recovered, but in truth he needed at least two weeks of rest, no arguments.
hunks.sol: It had only been a few days since Jopil’s brutal palm strike had left him with internal injuries. He had boasted to Jin Taekyung that he was almost fully recovered, but in truth, he needed at least two solid weeks of rest.

hunks.baseline: He was soaked through, and his legs were shaking.
hunks.sol: He was soaked through, and his legs were trembling.

hunks.baseline: He would have fallen behind even if he had only been trying to keep up. Carrying the solidly built Jin Taekyung on his back was literally killing him.
hunks.sol: He would have fallen behind even if he had only been trying to keep up. With the solidly built Jin Taekyung on his back, he was practically dying.

hunks.baseline: Now he was even hallucinating his parents—who were alive and well—waving him over. The woman standing beside them was a face he often saw at the temple hall.
hunks.sol: Now he was even hallucinating his parents—who were alive and well—beckoning to him. The woman standing beside them had a face he often saw in the temple hall.

hunks.baseline: “Child. You’ve suffered enough. You may rest now.”
hunks.sol: “Child. You have suffered enough. You may rest now.”

hunks.baseline: Her benevolent smile slowly eased Hyuk’s heart.
hunks.sol: Her benevolent smile slowly put Mujin’s heart at ease.

hunks.baseline: *Yeah. I’ve done enough. The squad leader collapses at the critical moment, and these bastards won’t even offer to carry him for me, whether I drop dead or not.*
hunks.sol: *Yeah. I’ve done enough. The squad leader drops like a rock when it matters most, and these bastards won’t even offer to carry him for me, whether I drop dead or not.*

hunks.baseline: Hyuk was just about to let go when—
hunks.sol: Mujin was just about to let go when—

hunks.baseline: Warm breath slipped into his ear. He knew who it was without turning around. Tears of relief stung Hyuk’s eyes.
hunks.sol: Warm breath tickled his ear. He knew who it was without turning around. Tears of relief sprang to Mujin’s eyes.

hunks.baseline: Blood and screams burst out on every side. A blood-soaked martial artist crawled on all fours between the corpses.
hunks.sol: Blood sprayed and screams rang out on every side. A blood-soaked martial artist crawled on all fours between the corpses.

hunks.baseline: His still-youthful face was stained with pain and terror.
hunks.sol: His still-youthful face was twisted with pain and terror.

hunks.baseline: He tried to hold it back, but the crying kept breaking free. He had spent ten years grinding through martial arts with grim determination, and it had all been useless on a battlefield spraying blood.
hunks.sol: He tried to hold it back, but the sobs kept breaking free. He had spent ten years gritting his teeth and honing his martial arts, yet none of it had helped him on this blood-soaked battlefield.

hunks.baseline: The senior he had counted on was dead. So was the comrade who had been like a brother. Weapons poured in from every direction, splitting open bellies and hacking limbs apart.
hunks.sol: The senior he had relied on was dead. So was the fellow disciple who had been like a brother. Weapons had poured in from every direction, splitting open bellies and hacking limbs apart.

hunks.baseline: He called for her without end, and then his face went stiff.
hunks.sol: He called for her over and over until his face suddenly went rigid.

hunks.baseline: A spearhead had already sprouted from his chest.
hunks.sol: A spearhead protruded from his chest.

hunks.baseline: His eyes flew wide for an instant, then the light went out of them. A wandering martial artist with a bandit’s beard pulled his rusty spear free and grinned.
hunks.sol: His eyes flew wide for an instant, then the light faded from them. A wandering martial artist with a bandit’s beard pulled his rusty spear free and grinned.

hunks.baseline: But even a wandering martial artist who had survived countless brushes with death could not dodge the blade that came flying at him a moment later.
hunks.sol: But even a wanderer who had survived countless brushes with death could not dodge the blade that came flying at him the next moment.

hunks.baseline: The Head Elder looked out over the battlefield, his face steeped in memory.
hunks.sol: The Head Elder gazed over the battlefield, lost in memory.

hunks.baseline: Eight Spring Gorge. A battleground that had occupied a single line in the history of the Great Faction War, decades ago. How many had died in that narrow gorge?
hunks.sol: Eight Spring Gorge. A battleground that had earned a single line in the history of the Great Faction War decades ago. How many people had died in that narrow gorge?

hunks.baseline: His body had been strong, and his heart had burned hot. It had been a time when that embarrassing character—chivalry—had still felt enormous.
hunks.sol: His body had been strong, and his heart had burned hot. Back then, the embarrassing word *chivalry* had still meant so much to him.

hunks.baseline: But the Great Faction War had changed the Head Elder. He had grown tired of the endless fighting, and afraid of death.
hunks.sol: But the Great Faction War had changed the Head Elder. He had grown weary of the endless fighting and afraid of death.

hunks.baseline: *What good is a chivalrous warrior? Die, and you’re nothing but a ghost.*
hunks.sol: *What good is being a chivalrous hero? Once you die, you’re nothing but a ghost.*

hunks.baseline: That had been a sliver of enlightenment. In the end he had survived and become a hero, and after a long stretch of endurance he had reached this place.
hunks.sol: That realization had been a form of enlightenment. In the end, he had survived and become a hero. After long years of patient endurance, he had finally reached this point.

hunks.baseline: The Head Elder turned his cunning old eyes on the man standing beside him.
hunks.sol: The Head Elder turned his shrewd old eyes toward the man standing beside him.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung was a remarkable talent. He was young, his martial arts were considerable, and above all he had the dignity and judgment a leader needed. He sometimes let himself be bound by sentiment, but perhaps because of that, he was deeply respected within the family.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung was a remarkable talent. He was young, highly accomplished in martial arts, and above all, possessed the dignity and judgment a leader needed. He sometimes allowed sentiment to sway him, but perhaps that was also why he was so deeply respected within the family.

hunks.baseline: *He’s more than capable of raising the family.*
hunks.sol: *He is more than capable of restoring this family.*

hunks.baseline: What a bizarre thing to be thinking, this far along. Jin Taekyung would already have died and become a lonely ghost, at that.
hunks.sol: What a ridiculous thing to be thinking after coming this far. Besides, Jin Taekyung was probably already dead, reduced to a lonely ghost.

hunks.baseline: “Nothing of importance. Old men talk to themselves more. More to the point, how does it look to you, Lesser Family Head?”
hunks.sol: “Nothing of importance. Old men tend to talk to themselves. More importantly, how does the battle look to you, Lesser Family Head?”

hunks.baseline: “The battle is going in our favor, but…”
hunks.sol: “It is going in our favor, but…”

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung’s expression darkened slightly. They held the advantage in troop quality and terrain, but the casualties kept mounting.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung’s expression darkened slightly. They held the advantage in troop quality and terrain, but their casualties continued to mount.

hunks.baseline: “A leader must know when to step forward. The longer the battle drags on, the more impatient they become. That is the moment we have to seize.”
hunks.sol: “A leader must know when to step forward. The longer the battle drags on, the more impatient the enemy will become. That is the moment we must seize.”

hunks.baseline: “If you, I, and Wipeng hold off the enemy command, and arrows rain down from the cliffs, their morale will hit rock bottom.”
hunks.sol: “If you, Wipeng, and I hold off the enemy commanders while arrows rain down from the cliffs, their morale will collapse.”

hunks.baseline: “It’s a shame we can’t use a fire attack. I resent the heavens.”
hunks.sol: “It’s a shame we can’t use fire. I resent the heavens.”

hunks.baseline: The narrow terrain of Eight Spring Gorge was perfect for fire, but the heavy snowfall from several days ago had left snowdrifts everywhere.
hunks.sol: The narrow terrain of Eight Spring Gorge was perfect for a fire attack, but the heavy snowfall several days ago had left snowdrifts everywhere.

hunks.baseline: Even if the heavens had taken Jin Wikyung’s side, though, what he was hoping for would never have happened.
hunks.sol: Yet even if the heavens had taken Jin Wikyung’s side, what he hoped for would never have happened.

hunks.baseline: The men drawing their bows on the cliffs would obey the Head Elder.
hunks.sol: The men drawing their bows atop the cliffs would obey the Head Elder’s command.

hunks.baseline: The years of waiting had been too long. He resented the destiny that had only now arrived.
hunks.sol: He had waited far too many years. He resented Heaven’s mandate for arriving only now.

hunks.baseline: The sight of Hyuk Mujin’s ugly face sent a rush of relief through me. The other reconnaissance squad members crowding in at the news that I was awake were no different.
hunks.sol: The sight of Hyuk Mujin’s ugly face filled me with relief. I felt the same way about the other reconnaissance squad members who crowded around after hearing I was awake.

hunks.baseline: But it was also a greeting I’d genuinely wanted to give them at least once.
hunks.sol: Still, it was a greeting I’d genuinely wanted to give them at least once.

hunks.baseline: …Not that they didn’t treat me like a lunatic afterward.
hunks.sol: …Even if it made them treat me like a lunatic.

hunks.baseline: “Anyway, that’s enough greeting. How long was I out?”
hunks.sol: “Anyway, that’s enough greetings. How long was I out?”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk dropped onto the ground with a thud and answered.
hunks.sol: Mujin dropped to the ground with a thud and answered.

hunks.baseline: “Definitely more than an hour, and a little under two.”
hunks.sol: “Definitely more than an hour, but probably a little under two.”

hunks.baseline: I’d spent two weeks in reality, so the timing roughly lined up. I nodded and moved on.
hunks.sol: I’d spent two weeks in reality, so the timing roughly lined up. I nodded and moved on to my next question.

hunks.baseline: “No time. Answer.”
hunks.sol: “We don’t have time. Just answer.”

hunks.baseline: “You were breathing, that’s why you woke up. Otherwise you’d be dead.”
hunks.sol: “You were breathing, so you woke up. Otherwise, you’d be dead.”

hunks.baseline: Apparently, logging in or logging out put the other side into a deathlike sleep.
hunks.sol: Apparently, logging in or out left my body on the other side in a state of suspended animation.

hunks.baseline: *If I’d logged out before dealing with the assassins, there wouldn’t have been a body to come back to.*
hunks.sol: *If I’d logged out before dealing with the assassins, there wouldn’t have been a body left for me to return to.*

hunks.baseline: “We were already heading that way. We split two men off and sent them back to the family.”
hunks.sol: “We were already heading toward them. I split off two men and sent them back to the family.”

hunks.baseline: “Uh, Captain. I’m sorry to say this, but… I think we have to consider the worst case.”
hunks.sol: “Uh, Captain. I’m sorry to say this, but… I think we have to consider the worst-case scenario.”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin and every member of the reconnaissance squad clamped their mouths shut. Nobody had to ask what the worst case meant.
hunks.sol: Mujin and every member of the reconnaissance squad fell silent. Nobody had to ask what the worst-case scenario meant.

hunks.baseline: *They read us completely.*
hunks.sol: *They saw through everything.*

hunks.baseline: Rage at losing his son and impatience with the situation had clouded his judgment. He had ignored his subordinates’ advice and taken the fastest route he could find.
hunks.sol: Rage over his son’s death and impatience with the situation had clouded his judgment. He had ignored his subordinates’ advice and chosen the fastest route.

hunks.baseline: And that was how he had run into the Jin Family of Taiyuan in a narrow gorge whose very name was unfamiliar: Eight Spring Gorge.
hunks.sol: And so he had encountered the Jin Family of Taiyuan in a narrow gorge whose very name had been unfamiliar to him: Eight Spring Gorge.

hunks.sol: The formidable eyesight of a Peak master pierced the battlefield.

hunks.sol: Well over a thousand of his men were trapped at the narrow entrance, unable to advance. The wandering martial artists and mounted bandits he had placed at the front had numbers, but individually, they were inferior even to the Jin Family’s rank-and-file warriors.
